A well flowing free, but no one drinks. My heart shrinks. Water can be drawn. The king makes a solemn covenant. All receive his blessings.
A well tiled. NO MISFORTUNE.
A well flowing clear. An icy spring. Drink.
A well drawn dry. Do not cover it. Sacrificing captives. MOST AUSPICIOUS.

statement: On a sacrifice day, use the captives. Supreme offering. Favourable augury. Troubles disappear.

lines.text: Binding with sandy-brown ox leather.
On a sacrifice day, bind it with leather. For an expedition: AUSPICIOUS. NO MISFORTUNE.
For an expedition: DISASTROUS. Augury: DANGEROUS. Leather harness with triple tassels. Sacrificing captives.
Troubles disappear. Sacrificing captives. For changing one’s orders: AUSPICIOUS.
Great men use tiger fur. Sacrificing captives before the augury is completed.
Princes use leopard fur, small men use raw leather. For an expedition: DISASTROUS. Augury for a dwelling: AUSPICIOUS.

statement: VERY AUSPICIOUS. Sacrifice.

lines.text: Tripod-bowl with up-turned feet: good for turning out bad meat. À slave-girl with a child to greet. NO MISFORTUNE.
Tripod-bowl full to the top. Illness makes my comrades drop; before it hits me, it will stop. AUSPICIOUS.
Tripod-bowl with lugs awry. Its proper use is blocked thereby, plump pheasant flesh left there to dry. Rain imminent. Trouble. Ultimately AUSPICIOUS.
Tripod-bowl with legs askew, spilling out the duke’s fine stew. Penalty of death is due. DISASTROUS.
Tripod-bowl with golden lugs and rod of bronze. Favourable augury.
Tripod-bowl with rod of jade. VERY AUSPICIOUS. Unfavourable for nothing.

statement: Offering. When thunder comes, crack-crack, there’s laughing chat, yack-yack. Though thunder frightens all the land, no drop of wine falls from the hand.

lines.text: After thunder comes, crack-crack, there’s laughing chat, yack-yack. AUSPICIOUS.
Risk and danger, thunder brings. Perhaps one loses cowrie-strings. Climbing the Nine Mounds, do not pursue. There’ll be restoration in seven days.
Thunder boonis and rumbles. Thunder when travelling: no catastrophe.
After thunder, mud.
Thunder goes and comes. DANGEROUS. There may be no loss. There is service.
When thunder splits the ear, folk look around ın fear. For an expedition: DISASTROUS. Thunder does not hit him, it hits his neighbours. NO MISFORTUNE. A wifes kin are grumbling.

statement: Cleaving the back to find nothing inside; crossing the court, where no one is spied. NO MISFORTUNE.

lines.text: Cleaving the feet. NO MISFORTUNE. Long-term augury favourable.
Cleaving the shins. Not removing the marrow. The heart is not pleased.
Cleaving the loın. Tearing the groin. DANGEROUS. Smoking heart.
Cleaving the trunk. NO MISFORTUNE.
Cleaving the jaw. Grumbling within the law. Troubles disappear.
Reaving, cleaving. AUSPICIOUS.

statement: Auspicious for a girls wedding. Favourable augury.

lines.text: Wild geese settling on the stream. Now a small one’s troubles teem. There are complaints. NO MISFORTUNE.
Wild geese settling on the rocks; feed and drink in honking flocks. AUSPICIOUS.
Wild geese settling on the shore. Her man is not yet back from war. She will bear no children more. DISASTROUS. Favourable against raiders.
Wild geese settling on the trees. They will roost there at their ease. NO MISFORTUNE.
Wild geese settling on the hill. The three-years’ bride, though barren still, will not be overcome by ill. AUSPICIOUS.
Wild geese settling on the peak. Their plumes for dancers’ use we’ll seek. AUSPICIOUS.

statement: For an expedition: DISASTROUS. Nothing favourable.

lines.text: A cousin given in marriage with companion-brides. Stepping out for feet that ail. For expeditions: AUSPICIOUS.
Sight returns for eyes that fail. Favourable augury for a prisoner.
A cousin given in marriage with her elder sister. Yet she marries with companion-brides.
A cousin given in marriage overruns her time: time for a delayed marriage.
Diyı gives his cousin in marriage. The sleeves of the bride are not so fine as the splendid sleeves of the concubine. The moon waxes full. AUSPICIOUS.
The bride bears a skip, but it holds no fruit. The groom stabs a sheep, but no blood will shoot. Nothing favourable.

statement: Sacrifice. The king is present. Do not grieve. Appropriate for the middle of the day.

lines.text: Meeting the mistress of the house. For a ten-day week, NO MISFORTUNE. Leaving means receiving.
Thick is the screen. Seeing the Plough at noon. Departing brings risk of illness. Sacrificing captives who plead submission. AUSPICIOUS.
Thick are the pennons. At noon jaint light is made. Breaking the right arm, NO MISFORTUNE.
Thick 1s the screen. Seeing the Plough at noon. Meeting the master now.
Though hindrance come, None will be glum. Praise. AUSPICIOUS.
Thick ls the roof screening the house. Peep through the door: no one is there. Not seen for several years. DISASTROUS.

statement: Lesser offering. Augury for sojourners: AUSPICIOUS.

lines.text: A sojourner smashes the place to smithereens. Bringing catastrophe.
A sojourner comes to rest, his goods enfolded to his breast. Getting servant boys. Augury: AUSPICIOUS.
A sojourner burns the lodging place. Losing his servant boys. Augury DANGEROUS.
A sojourner finds a place to stay, and stows his travelling-axe. My heart rests not.
A pheasant is got with a single shot. Disappearing. Ultimately with a decree of honour.
A bird destroys its nursery; A sojourner first laughs with glee, then weeps and moans in misery. Loss of oxen in Yi. DISASTROUS.

statement: Lesser offering. Favourable when there is somewhere to go. Favourable for seeing great men.

lines.text: Advancing and retreating. Augury favourable for military men.
Food offerings set out before an altar. Use large numbers of diviners and shamans. AUSPICIOUS. NO MISFORTUNE.
Setting out food offerings side by side. Distress.
Troubles disappear. Three kinds of game caught in one hunt.
Augury AUSPICIOUS. Troubles disappear. Unfavourable for nothing. No beginning, but there will be an end. Three days before a geng day and three days after: AUSPICIOUS.
Food offerings set out before an altar. Losing a travelling-axe. Augury DISASTROUS.

statement: Offering. Favourable augury.

lines.text: Satisfaction in peacemaking. AUSPICIOUS.
Satisfaction in taking captives. AUSPICIOUS. Troubies disappear.
Satisfaction to come. DISASTROUS.
Satisfaction in rewards. No peace yet. Disease confined, the outcome will be happy.
Captives go for flaying. It will be DANGEROUS.
Lasting satisfaction.

statement: Offering. The king is present in the ancestral temple. Favourable for fording a big river. Favourable augury.

lines.text: For gelding a horse: healıng. AUSPICIOUS.
Gushing over the stable. Troubles disappear.
Gushing on the body. No trouble.
Gushing over the bystanders. MOST AUSPICIOUS. Gushing on to their mound. Can such things be found?
Gushing, flushing the liver. A great scream. Gushing in the king’s dwelling. NO MISFORTUNE.
Gushing, this blood of castration. In going fa, NO MISFORTUNE.

statement: Offering. Bitter juncture. Augury not possible.

lines.text: Not going out of the door to the courtyard. NO MISFORTUNE.
Not going out of the gate of the courtyard. DISASTER.
Not gauging the juncture. Sighing. NO MISFORTUNE.
Secure juncture. Offering.
Satisfactory juncture. AUSPICIOUS. Leaving means receiving.
Bitter juncture. Augury: DISASTROUS. Troubles disappear.

statement: Good fortune. AUSPICIOUS. Favourable for fording a big river. Favourable augury.

lines.text: Requiem sacrifice. AUSPICIOUS. There will be unexpected calamity. No feast.
A crane calls on a shaded slope, its chicks call in reply. Here we have a brimming cup: together we'll drink it dry.
Taking the foe. Great drums thud, tabor-beats surge; Some fall to weeping, some start a dirge.
The moon will soon be fully round. One horse’s yoke-mate can’t be found. NO MISFORTUNE.
Sacrificing captives, bound together. NO MISFORTUNE.
A sound of pinions rising to the sky. Augury DISASTROUS.

statement: Offering. Favourable augury. Right for small matters, not right for large matters. À flying bird leaves a sound. Not appropriate to go up; appropriate to go down. VERY AUSPICIOUS.

lines.text: Flying bird. Therefore: DISASTER.
Passing a forefather, coming to a foremother; Not reaching the prince, meeting the minister. NO MISFORTUNE.
Not passing. Beware one passing on the track, Lest he stab you in the back. DISASTER.
NO MISFORTUNE. Not passing, meeting. Going is dangerous. Need to keep alert. Not for use in long-term augury.
Thick clouds, no rain, from our western suburbs. The duke harpoons a bird, retrieving it from a cave.
Not meeting, passing. A flying bird ts netted. DISASTER. This means catastrophic calamity.

statement: Offering. Somewhat favourable augury. Auspicious at the beginning, confused at the end.

lines.text: ‘Trailing a cord. Soaking the tail. NO MISFORTUNE.
A lady loses an ornamental hairpin. Not seeking it, getting it in Seven days.
Gaozong quelled Guifang, overcoming it in three years. Not for use with small men.
A tunic padded with silk wadding. Stay dlert all day long.
Eastern neighbours slay an ox; not like the western neighbours’ surimet sacrifice. Truly receiving their blessings.
Getting the head wet. DANGEROUS.

statement: Offering. Not quite across the water yet, the young fox gets its tail-tip wet. Favourable for nothing.

lines.text: Getting the tail wet. Distress.
‘Trailing a cord. AUSPICIOUS.
Not yet across. Disastrous for expeditions. Favourable for fording a big river.
Augury AUSPICIOUS. Troubles disappear. This is how Zhen quelled Guifang, and in three years won gifts from Shang.
Augury AUSPICIOUS. No troubles. Glory for princes. Sacrificing captives. AUSPICIOUS.
Sacrificing captives at a wine-drinking. NO MISFORTUNE. Getting the head wet. Sacrificing captives. Losing a spoon.
